The Devil Wears Prada Ending Explained: Andy's Big Choice

Key Takeaways for Readers

  • Andy Sachs abandons Runway's cutthroat orbit to reclaim her journalistic integrity in New York.
  • Meryl Streep and Emily Blunt deliver iconic, career-defining comedic and dramatic performances.
  • The iconic fountain scene in Paris remains a definitive cinematic statement on workplace burnout.
  • A sharp 7.4/10 audience favorite that holds up remarkably well nearly two decades later.
🎯 AUDIENCE & WATCHLIST GUIDE
✓ Who Will Love This:

Fans of razor-sharp workplace satire, iconic fashion design, and powerhouse female-led dramedies.

⚠️ Who Should Pass:

You are looking for a gritty drama rather than a glossy, fast-paced mid-2000s comedy-drama.

From Skeptical Outsider to Haute Couture

Fresh out of Northwestern with literary ambitions, Andy Sachs lands a coveted role at Runway purely as a career stepping stone. Flung into the razor-sharp universe of high fashion, she quickly clashes with Miranda Priestly's impossible demands and the hyper-competitive atmosphere maintained by senior assistant Emily. Andy gradually trades her frumpy sweaters for Chanel boots and runway samples, gaining Miranda's elusive approval. Yet her meteoric rise comes at a punishing personal cost, steadily alienating her boyfriend Nate and closest friends as Runway's relentless demands swallow her identity.

The Paris Climax and Fountain Drop Explained

During Paris Fashion Week, Andy glimpses the cold reality of Miranda's ruthless survival instincts when the editor blindsides Nigel to protect her own throne. Miranda points out that Andy did the exact same thing by stepping over Emily to secure the Paris trip, observing that they share identical ambition. Terrified of transforming into the callous woman sitting beside her, Andy makes her fateful stand. In broad daylight, she tosses her ringing company phone into the Place de la Concorde fountain, severing ties with the toxic machine to chase authentic journalism on her own terms.

Streep, Hathaway, and Backstage Magic

Director David Frankel struck lightning with this ensemble. Meryl Streep made the inspired artistic choice to play Miranda with a hushed, icy whisper rather than furious shouting, making every cutting remark lethal. Anne Hathaway balances vulnerability and poise, while Emily Blunt's frantic, scene-stealing energy launched her into mainstream Hollywood stardom. Stanley Tucci anchors the production with weary warmth as Nigel, lending heart to Patricia Field's jaw-dropping costume design, which transformed Manhattan into an intoxicating, high-stakes runway of couture.

Critical Reception and Enduring Appeal

Boasting a strong 7.4/10 score among cinephiles, the film remains an essential modern comedy-drama. Holding a PG-13 rating for mild language and adult workplace situations, it serves as sharp entertainment for teens and adults alike. While modern viewers frequently debate Nate's unsupportive behavior and the toxicity of 2000s hustle culture, the movie's razor-sharp dialogue, impeccable pacing, and biting industry satire ensure it stays endlessly rewatchable on home streaming platforms.
